text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, which saves time for everyone working on the project. One key part of clean code is following naming conventions. Variables and functions should have clear, meaningful names, so others can understand what they do without extra explanation. Another important idea is keeping functions small and focused on one task. This makes the code simpler and easier to test. Finally, clean code is easier to maintain. When code is well organized, fixing bugs and adding new features becomes much faster. In short, writing clean code helps teams work better together.
